title: Patrick B NDE 3384
content: It was a January day in Michigan, rather cold and snowy. There was a coating of melted snow that had been left behind by the snow plow in the parking lot, as the wind blew across the lot it froze all that was left behind. At some point, some associates and I were outside enjoying the snow like children. A game of football was started with a frozen ball of snow. I received a pass and was tackled by one of the guys. I slipped on one of those patches of frozen snow and fell backwards hitting my head on the ice and pavement. I was out cold. As I can recall I remember seeing myself lying there, I could hear everyone around me freaking out because I wouldn't wake up. At one point one of the guys said 'His lips are turning blue. We better call 911.' All this time I could hear and see everything as though I was standing in the crowd. The emergency medical technicians showed up and began working on me. As they were doing their job I remember feeling a rush of warmth come over me, but looking down I could see how cold and lifeless my body looked, I really thought nothing of it I was completely comfortable just seeing what was going on. The really freaky part came when they put me in the ambulance I actually went with my body to the hospital all the while being able to hear everything around me and see it very clearly. I remember what seemed to be emotions although it felt as if I was pulled in two different directions at once. One saying stay and the other saying I must go. No sooner than that I was back in my body in when I was at the local hospital.

out_of_body.vantage_other_detail: He perceived events as though he was standing in the crowd, and also accompanied his body in the ambulance to the hospital.
out_of_body.separation_sensations_other: Felt a 'rush of warmth' while observing his body as cold and lifeless; felt pulled in two directions (stay vs. must go).

context.nde_cause_other_detail: Slipped on frozen snow/ice while playing with a frozen snowball and hit his head on ice/pavement; unconscious ('out cold').

stage_sequence.elements_other_detail: Emotional sense of being pulled in two directions ('stay' vs. 'must go') while observing events around his unconscious body and during ambulance transport.
stage_sequence.sequence_variation_description: OBE at the scene, continued perception during ambulance transport, then sudden return to body at the hospital; no tunnel/light/realm described.

unique_elements.nonstandard_elements: He reports accompanying his physical body to the hospital in the ambulance while remaining out-of-body and perceiving events clearly.
unique_elements.notable_quotes: “His lips are turning blue. We better call 911.”; “I remember feeling a rush of warmth come over me”; “it felt as if I was pulled in two different directions at once. One saying stay and the other saying I must go.”
